To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the internal rotation of a water molecule in the indole(H$_2$O) cluster can be described by a two-state model, and the coupling of the overall rotation and the internal rotation is small for typical field strengths and pulse lengths in the experiments, and can therefore be neglected.

for typical field-strengths in alignment and mixed field orientation experiments the internal and overall rotations of the investigated cluster can be treated separately and that the internal rotations can be described by a rigid rotor.
the rigid rotor approximation for describing rotational dynamics of the investigated cluster is valid for typical field strengths of alignment and mixed-field rotation experiments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of theoretical and computational tools for the investigation of the dynamics of molecular clusters.
the dynamics of the $\text{indol}(\text{D}_2\text O)$ cluster.

the development of a computational tool that can be used to describe laser-induced molecular dynamics of weakly bound clusters, and that allows to predict the outcome of alignment and mixed-field rotation experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the internal and overall rotational motions of the $\text{indol}(\text{OH}_2)$ molecular cluster can be treated separately for field strengths up to $E_{0} \approx 1.5 \times 10^{8} \text{V/m}$, which is the maximum value of the electric field strength that can be achieved in the laboratory.
the internal and overall rotational dynamics of $\text{indol}(\text{D}_2\text O)$ are not coupled for the typical field strength of alignment and mixed-field experiments.

the rigid rotor approximation for the internal rotation is valid for field strengths up to 1.5 $\times$ 10$^9$ $\text{V}/\text{cm}$, which is well within the range of field strengths typically employed in alignment and mixed field orientation experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the internal rotation of water in $\text{indol}(\text{HO})$ can be treated independently from the overall rotational motion of the cluster, and that the internal rotation can be treated within the rigid rotor approximation.

the internal rotation of a weakly bound water molecule can be neglected in the context of laser-induced alignment and mixed-field rotational orientation experiments, and that this approximation is valid over a wide range of experimental parameters.
the internal rotation of a weakly bound water molecule can be neglected in the description of laser-induced alignment and mixed-field orientational dynamics of a $\text{indol}(\text{water})$ cluster.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the internal dynamics of the $\text{indol}(\text{water})$ molecular cluster are not significantly altered by the external field and that this system can thus be treated as a rigid rotor.
the internal dynamics can be safely neglected in alignment and orientation experiments, as long as the field strength is below a certain threshold.
the internal rotation of water is only marginally affected by the external electric field and that the internal rotation is not a significant source of decoherence for overall rotation.
